name: openshapeforge
//overrides: Both entries lift a transitive pin inside `next` that carries fixed CVEs.
postcss: next pins 8.4.31 exactly, so it cannot float; 8.5.x is a minor
and @tailwindcss/postcss already requires ^8.5.16, so this de-duplicates
the tree rather than adding to it.
sharp: an optional dependency next uses for image optimisation. Nothing
here imports next/image, so it is unused — the bump is free.
Drop an entry once next ships a release that pins the fixed version.
//devDependencies: Root-level only so `examples/tsconfig.json` can resolve Bun's globals. @types/bun is otherwise hoisted under apps/api, which nothing outside apps/api can resolve from.

scripts.typecheck:compiler: bun run check:ts-nocheck && bun run --cwd packages/compiler typecheck
scripts.//typecheck:admin: The control-plane app (apps/admin). Its own gate rather than part of typecheck:web: separate Next project, separate tsconfig, and nothing under apps/admin is compiler output — so unlike apps/web, a type error here is a bug in this repo's hand-written code and never something to fix in packages/compiler.
scripts.//typecheck:examples: The shipped example plugins and connectors, which apps/api and packages/compiler both exclude — plugin runtime code the API imports at boot was untypechecked until this existed. tsc comes from apps/api because it is the workspace that depends on it.
scripts.//typecheck:connectors: The shipped connector packages, which moved out of examples/ when connectors became a top level directory. Same reason typecheck:examples exists: apps/api and packages/compiler both exclude them, so nothing else reads them as source.
scripts.//typecheck:layout: packages/workflow-layout has its own tsconfig — no DOM lib, stricter than the app's — so it cannot be folded into typecheck:web. Its own gate, run alongside the others.
scripts.//typecheck:plugin-web: The workflow plugin's web half: browser code, so browser resolution. Separate from typecheck:examples, whose NodeNext settings would demand .js specifiers Turbopack cannot resolve.
scripts.//test:connectors: ./connectors and not connectors: bun test treats a bare argument as a path SUBSTRING, so `bun test connectors` also sweeps apps/api/src/connectors and reports its pre-existing failures as this suite's.
scripts.//dev:admin: The control plane, on port 3002. Not a free choice: the control realm allow-lists http://localhost:3002/* as the openshapeforge-admin-gateway client's only app redirect URI, so another port fails at Keycloak rather than at the app. Needs the compose stack up (Keycloak on 8181 with the openshapeforge-control realm imported, and Redis for the session store).
scripts.//test:browser: The browser suite for apps/web. Unlike every other test script here it needs a RUNNING stack — Postgres, Redis, Keycloak, apps/api and apps/web — because it signs in through the real Keycloak login page and drives the assembled screen. See apps/web/playwright.config.ts and .github/workflows/web-e2e.yml.
scripts.//notices:linux: Regenerates the committed notices on the platform CI checks. The tree has platform-native optional packages, so a macOS run emits darwin variants and fails check:notices. An anonymous container volume keeps the Linux install separate from the caller's node_modules, preventing a cross-platform union and preserving the local workspace. See the script header.
scripts.notices:linux: docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 -v "$PWD":/w -v /w/node_modules -w /w oven/bun:1.3.4 sh -c 'bun install --frozen-lockfile >/dev/null 2>&1 && bun scripts/gen-third-party-notices.ts'
scripts.//check:notices:linux: The gate as CI runs it, from any platform. Plain check:notices compares against THIS machine's install, so on a Mac it reports the darwin natives as drift and can never pass — use this before opening a PR. Its temporary Linux node_modules volume leaves the local workspace intact.
scripts.check:notices:linux: docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 -v "$PWD":/w -v /w/node_modules -w /w oven/bun:1.3.4 sh -c 'bun install --frozen-lockfile >/dev/null 2>&1 && bun scripts/gen-third-party-notices.ts --check'
